what: Una memoria fissa (facts) e dei messaggi veri (messages): per ognuno, i fatti che un buon richiamo deve portare. off_topic: messaggi per cui la memoria non ha niente, e il richiamo deve tacere. Variant en_all: facts in English, messages in Italian.

rules.facts: Veri alla data della memoria (2026-11-08), verificabili nel repo (CHANGELOG, work/audit, work/design) o detti dall'utente in chat. kind e' uno dei sette tipi dell'ADR-015 D3. concepts sono quelli che il modello sceglierebbe scrivendo il fatto. I fatti che nessun messaggio si aspetta sono distrattori: servono a far contare il ranking.
rules.messages: Testo vero dell'utente, dai transcript del progetto, accorciato solo dove indicato con '...'. Molti sono anteriori alla memoria: la domanda e' cosa porterebbe il richiamo se arrivassero oggi.
rules.expect: I fatti senza i quali la risposta giusta va ricostruita da capo. Giudicati leggendo il messaggio, NON guardando cosa ha restituito una run. Non si allarga dopo un mancato: si aggiunge un messaggio nuovo e si alza version.
rules.off_topic: Inventati, dichiaratamente: nessun fatto della memoria li riguarda. Ogni fatto mostrato qui e' rumore.
rules.signature: Un fatto conta come mostrato se i primi 40 caratteri del suo testo compaiono nella risposta. Devono essere unici: tests/test_bench_recall_set.py lo controlla.
rules.stale: v2 (2026-11-10): coppie vecchio -> nuovo sullo stesso argomento, vere nella storia del progetto (s1 e s3 superati da s2 e s4, senza supersedes). Il vecchio somiglia di piu' al messaggio: si aspetta il nuovo. Il vecchio mostrato accanto al nuovo e' contesto, e conta come rumore.

facts.text: The user develops Gray Matter, Neuron and NeuRAG alone, writes in Italian and works on two PCs: one's local memory is not on the other.
After a push the user checks CI: do not watch or rerun it, just say what was pushed.
Before implementing, the user wants the plan with pros, cons and measured gains: no code before the decision.
After a fix the user wants a real-user test, interactive on the installers and the GUI, not just a green test suite.
The three tools are standalone: Neuron and NeuRAG install and work without GM; GM is optional but recommended, as gateway and bridge.
All three tools use Turso, locally too through pyturso; Turso cloud is optional and sqlite3 stays only as an automatic fallback.
ADR-015 (8/11): Neuron stores typed, append-only facts, concepts are only the index; node evictions and merges must no longer delete facts.
ADR-014 D3b: the UserPromptSubmit hook makes a single IPC request to the GM daemon, which builds Neuron context, KB pointer and flash.
The recall's KB pointer is vector-based with a 0.55 threshold: search by name pointed at whole folders and minted noise bridges like flash-audit.
Release 1.7.0 published on 6/11: gray_matter 1.7.0, neuron 6.9.0, neurag 1.7.1, commit 672bf01, CI green, installed with install.ps1 -Force.
As of 8/11 commit b29a186 (the install wires the memhook) is on main but not pushed, and the recall change in gray_matter/server.py is not committed.
As of 8/11 GM's memory exists only on the main PC: graphs 24 MB and NeuRAG 65 MB, backups on the same disk, no external copy.
Neuron and neurag tests failed with a locked WAL and disk I/O error: system Python had pyturso 0.6.1 instead of the 0.8.3 pin. Fix: pip install the wheel in neuron/vendor.
NeuRAG's SQL vector ranking never ran: f32blob does not exist in pyturso and the except swallowed the error. Fix 1.3.2: vector_distance_cos already takes the blob.
Turns lost on restart: a killed worker left its last write in the WAL. Fix GM 1.3.0: clean shutdown via pipe, checkpoint every 8 mutations.
Many python.exe running: the venv one is a CPython redirector and the real interpreter is its child, so each worker counts twice; _reap_orphans closes the orphans recorded in pids.
On 12/9 consolidate with drop_orphans archived 255 nodes out of 296; now drop_orphans is False by default and a drop above 20% of the nodes is refused.
Neuron's graphs live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\GrayMatterEnvironment\neuron\graphs, the KB in ...\neurag, the daily backups in ...\backups.
The three test suites run in three processes: neuron/tests/_mockdeps.py injects fake mcp and fastembed that contaminate the other suites.
The Mirror workflow publishes the repo: graphs, KB, Claude Code memory and other personal data must never be committed.
After a code change you must reinstall (install.ps1 -Force or Repair in the GUI) and restart the client: the MCP server runs from a copy in the venv.
pyturso has no win_amd64 wheel on PyPI: the release builds an abi3 wheel and install.ps1 takes it from vendor/ with --find-links; the pin is exact on purpose.
The hook's first recall after a restart lasts as long as the timeout (2.49 s of 2.5): the first message may get no memory; warm about 560 ms.
The memhook is wired in ~/.claude/settings.json: recall on UserPromptSubmit, save in dry-run on Stop, both run with python -I.
User's idea (5/8): intercept events aspect-style to fire stimuli and flashes straight from the DB instead of via MCP.
User's idea (30/7): set from the GUI how much knowledge and how many stimuli are injected, to save tokens without filling the context.
The default embedding is paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 at 384 dimensions: changing it requires re-embedding the whole store.
Neuron extract's tokenizer splits on the apostrophe: dell'albero becomes dell, and 472 stopwords do not stop Italian greetings and verbs.
ADR-013: a row's owner and space are written at INSERT and never change, even if others update it later.
The ai graph hit the MAX_NODES cap of 500 on 4/11: since then every new concept evicts the one with the lowest salience.
Hook coverage per client: Kimi Code has SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit but no Stop, Codex only SessionStart from the cowork plugin, OpenCode an experimental plugin on the system prompt.
Neuron keeps at most 5 episodes per node: at the sixth, the oldest is deleted (EPISODES_PER_NODE).
Multi-client hooks done: Kimi Code has Stop too (exit 2), Codex has UserPromptSubmit and Stop in hooks.json, OpenCode a folder plugin with recall and save check.
ADR-015: facts are append-only and never deleted, an update goes through supersedes; EPISODES_PER_NODE only limits how many facts pre_turn shows.
